guide: Set up error monitoring so you hear about a broken site from an alert, not from a user. You need a live app, a free Sentry account and Claude Code or Codex.
1. Create a Sentry account and add a new project for your app's framework (Next.js, React, Node and so on).
1. Run Sentry's setup wizard from your project folder, which installs the SDK and adds the config files for you.
1. Add your project's Sentry DSN to your hosting provider's environment variables, for example in Vercel.
1. Deploy, then trigger a deliberate error on a page to confirm it appears in Sentry's Issues list.
1. Turn on uptime monitoring for your live URL so Sentry alerts you when the site stops responding.
1. Connect alerts to email or Slack so a failure reaches you the moment it happens.
1. Test it the way I did: pause the site, wait for the uptime alert, then bring it back.
Watch out: passing tests only prove the cases you thought of, so don't treat a green test run as the same thing as watching the live site.

```
You are helping me add error and uptime monitoring to my live web app using Sentry. My app is built with <framework, for example Next.js> and hosted on <hosting provider, for example Vercel>. I use <Claude Code or Codex> and can run commands in my project folder.
Please do the following:
1. Explain how to create a Sentry project for <framework> and where to find the DSN.
2. Give me the exact command for Sentry's setup wizard and tell me which files it will change.
3. Show where to set the DSN as an environment variable on <hosting provider>, and make sure no secret is committed to my repository.
4. Add a small test route or button that throws a deliberate error, so I can confirm Sentry receives it.
5. Explain how to set up uptime monitoring for <my live URL> and how to send alerts to <email or Slack>.
6. Give me a short checklist to test it end to end, including pausing the site to check the uptime alert fires.
Keep changes minimal, explain each step in plain English, and finish by listing every file you changed.
```
